summary: Request: Align rate-plan refill semantics for mixed webhook callback + embedding bulk orchestration to avoid post-upgrade 429 waves
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports recurring 429 throttles immediately after a billing/tier upgrade and an orchestrator migration. Traffic mix: long-lived SSE sessions for real-time UI updates + high-throughput background workers that bulk-upload embeddings (multipart). Both flows use the same API key prefix but different routes.

Impact:
- NovaLens engineers see 10-20% of requests return 429s for 10-30 minutes after upgrade/migration windows.
- Real-time UI sessions are affected (SSE disconnects) causing poor UX; background embedding pipeline stalls and retries, increasing cost.

Environment / context:
- Private tenant on dedicated capacity (enterprise).
- Orchestrator migrated from a single long-lived API key per pod to ephemeral subkeys for per-worker identity last week.
- Tier upgraded from dedicated-standard -> enterprise-plus earlier today.
- Edge proxies in us-west cache refill counters for rate windows for up to ~90s.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start bulk embedding backfill (500 concurrent chunk uploads across 20 workers).
2) Open 200 SSE connections from UI clients multiplexed through an ingress layer.
3) Trigger billing tier update in Console (simulate upgrade).
4) Observe 429 waves on SSE endpoints and chunk upload endpoints immediately after upgrade and for ~15-25 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- Throttles occur at both route and tenant layers.
- Throttle headers sometimes show different windows depending on which edge served the client.
- Console shows quota refreshed, but edge metrics show stale refill counters and sudden token depletion events.

Expected behavior:
- Tier upgrade should refresh refill rates consistently across edge and origin within a short reconciliation window without producing opaque 429 waves for mixed traffic patterns.

Attachments:
- Customer's packet capture snippets and sampled throttle headers (provided in ticket attachments).
- App logs showing SSE reconnects and embedding worker retry backoff traces.

investigation_notes: Checked edge refill drift: grafana panels show some edges had stale refill counters for up to 2m after upgrade (query: rate_limiter.refill_counter{edge_group="usw"} offset 120s).

Observed double-accounting traces where preflight checks and signed-url callback endpoints incremented tenant-level counters and per-route counters because of shared API key prefix + missing route-isolation header.

Hypothesis 1: Tier upgrade triggers origin refill immediate delta but edges apply refill at window boundaries and do not reconcile outstanding token deficits until next tick, causing a sawtooth exhaustion for mixed long-lived and burst flows.

Hypothesis 2: Orchestrator's move to ephemeral keys created many short-lived tokens that were not correctly associated with dedicated burst pools, amplifying aggregate token consumption in the first 30s after migration.

Runbook actions taken: purged edge refill cache for edge-usw-03 and edge-usw-12; triggered refill-broadcast job (internal job id: rb-20241115-9). Confirmed transient drop in 429s for new connections immediately post-action.

Collected logs: ingress-proxy logs show repeated 429 responses with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Window: 10s; some clients had mismatched X-Forwarded-Proto and x-client-id missing causing route misattribution.

Telemetry note: token accounting spike correlated with a background health-check sweep from a subservice (dynamo-ingest) that resumed heavy pinging during the upgrade window - we flagged this as contributing factor.
Related GH PR addresses refill propagation ordering and makes the refill broadcast idempotent and immediate for tier changes. Also includes a metric to surface 'edge-refill-lag' in Console.
resolution:
Workaround applied and permanent remediation planned:

Temporary workarounds performed:
- Purged edge refill caches for affected edge-usw instances (reduced immediate 429s).
- Created an isolated burst pool for SSE route and promoted priority-class for real-time connections to avoid interference with bulk embedding traffic.
- Guided customer to add explicit X-Client-ID header on signed-url callbacks so requests are attributed to the correct route.

Permanent fixes / follow-ups:
- Merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rl-rate-limiter/pull/421 to make tier-change refill propagation immediate and idempotent; rolling to staging tomorrow and to production in the next deploy window.
- Add server-side guard to map ephemeral subkeys to the correct burst pool on key creation to avoid initial fanout overcount. (Engineering task created, linked: INT-80422).
- Update Console to show 'edge-refill-lag' metric and display advisory on plan changes (docs task: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/644321/Rate+Pool+Design).
- Support runbook updated to include 'edge purge + refill push' steps during customer tier upgrades and migrations.

Customer outcomes:
- Customer confirmed mitigation reduced 429s to <1% and embedding backfill completed successfully. They requested follow-up notification when the permanent fix is live and documentation updates are available.

Follow-up actions (owners):
- Rate-limiter team to monitor rollout (Ian Park).
- SRE to automate edge-refill-push on tier change events (Ethan Rivera).
- Docs to add guidance for customers performing orchestrator migrations/ephemeral-key rollouts (Maya Chen).
